from math import gcd


def best_average(a: list[int], k: int) -> list[int]:
    n = len(a)
    P = [0] * (n + 1)
    for i, x in enumerate(a):
        P[i + 1] = P[i] + x

    # Start from the whole array's average, reduced to lowest terms.
    p, q = P[n], n
    g = gcd(p, q)
    p, q = p // g, q // g

    # Dinkelbach iteration: with current ratio p/q, find a subarray with
    # length >= k maximizing sum - (p/q) * len, scaled by q to stay integral.
    # If the maximum is positive, its average strictly exceeds p/q; repeat.
    while True:
        best_val = 0
        best_pair = None
        min_f = None
        min_i = -1
        for j in range(k, n + 1):
            i = j - k
            fi = q * P[i] - p * i
            if min_f is None or fi < min_f:
                min_f = fi
                min_i = i
            fj = q * P[j] - p * j
            v = fj - min_f
            if v > best_val:
                best_val = v
                best_pair = (min_i, j)
        if best_pair is None:
            break
        i, j = best_pair
        s = P[j] - P[i]
        length = j - i
        g = gcd(s, length)
        p, q = s // g, length // g

    return [p, q]
